items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I don't know if you saw the Spike Lee film or saw portions of it, but it is really a devastating experience just to see entire neighborhoods wiped off the face of the earth you know.

ctx.x: Leaves. Like I had like leaves like I live under these oak trees I mean it’s a beautiful street it’s like this avenue. And it’s like these 300 year old oak trees. Some of them fell obviously from the wind breaking, but what happened was all of the wind just pushed all the leaves on my front porch. I’m telling you man, I had to like open the gate, move a tree branch, move the leaves out of the way, it was incredible, and open up my front door and I thought I was going to smell this wretched smell coming through my…

of my house and that was it, you know, decorative tiles on my roof. That was it. I mean I was thankful. I mean in relation to everybody else who lost everything. My parents lost their houses, my sisters lost their houses, only one brother, believe it or not who lived in a part of town that really flooded but his house was fine. But it was unbelievable, truly. I mean until you see it for yourself or saw it for yourself during that time you would have thought an atomic bomb had been dropped in New Orleans, it was…
